title: Binary Digital Clock
intro: This clock displays ordinary local civil hours, minutes and seconds in base two. It changes the notation, not the length of the day or the units of time.
structure: The hour has five binary digits (weights 16, 8, 4, 2, 1). Minutes and seconds have six digits (weights 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1). Read each field as the sum of the weights whose digit is 1. Leading zeros remain visible.
example: 13:45:09 is 01101:101101:001001. The hour is 8+4+1, the minutes are 32+8+4+1 and the seconds are 8+1. Midnight is 00000:000000:000000.
history: Binary notation is a modern alternative presentation of conventional time, not an ancient civil timekeeping system. This is whole-field binary, not binary-coded decimal digits.
model: The provider obtains the local day phase in microseconds, floors to ordinary seconds and extracts hours, minutes and seconds by integer division and remainder. Each complete field is encoded independently in binary. The optional seconds field and vertical presentation are supported. The next visible update is the next ordinary second or minute boundary, rounded up to milliseconds.
limits: Requires the caller's civil offset; it does not require geographic coordinates or change stored timestamps. Valid hour values stop at 23 and minute/second values at 59, even though the bit fields could represent larger values.
